newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees '97 primary surplus at 1.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees '97 primary surplus at 1.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan said he expects the country to post a primary budget surplus of 1.5 percent of gross domestic product in 1997.
In 1996, Brazil registered a primary budget deficit of 0.09 percent of GDP.
The primary budget result does not include interest payments on government debt.
Malan, speaking at a seminar on private savings, also said that operational and nominal deficits this year would be lower than in 1996. He did not elaborate.
Last year, Brazil posted an operational deficit of 3.89 percent of GDP. The operational result includes government debt servicing costs.
